Meeting header: 2026-04-09 16:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Jordan Ellis, Priya Rao (Redwood); Tomás Rivera, Maya Chen, Leila Park, Abe Novak (Ember)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for doing this kickoff, um, appreciate you carving out time. Quick intros?
[00:08] Tomás (Ember CTO): Hi, Tomas here, CTO at Ember Systems. We're building a vector search + LLM layer for customer support automation, looking to validate inference economics and compliance posture.
[00:20] Maya (Head of Security): Maya, head of security. My priorities: SOC 2, ISO where applicable, SSO, RBAC and strong audit trails.
[00:28] Leila (ML Platform): Leila, ML Platform. I'll own the workload side—prompt sets, traces, perf metrics.
[00:34] Jordan: Great. Priya is our SE, she'll drive the benchmark plan.
[00:38] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks. Brief agenda: align on acceptance criteria, go over security asks, define workload sizing and bench targets, and then timeline.
[00:47] Tomás: Sounds good. For context, our current latency p95 is about 180 ms for small-ish models but with our homegrown infra; for larger sequences we see spikes up to 700 to 900ms. Our traffic profile is bursty—user facing queries ~60 reqs/s at peak across two regions.
[01:05] Priya: Ok, that helps. For the POC we should aim to replicate representative workload—what token lengths are we seeing?
[01:12] Leila: Median 150 tokens, 95th around 2,500 tokens for long context retrieval. Most of the embed + generate flow ends up with 600–1k tokens.
[01:22] Priya: Great — we'll include runs at 150, 1k, and 2.5k tokens.
[01:27] Jordan: On the security side, Maya, can you run us through your must-haves?
[01:31] Maya: Sure. Must-haves: SOC 2 Type II report or attestation in progress, ISO 27001 scope or plan, SSO via SAML compatible with Okta, RBAC so we can restrict access at team level, immutable audit logs with retention policy we can set, KMS/HSM for key management, and network isolation options—VPC peering or private deployment. Also need to know data residency options.
[01:52] Jordan: Makes sense — we have SOC 2 Type II for our hosted control plane, ISO 27001 in progress, SAML SSO via Okta supported, and RBAC on Console. Audit logs are available; retention is configurable depending on plan — default 90 days, enterprise 1 year plus exports to S3. We use customer-managed KMS in Private deployments.
[02:12] Maya: Ok, can you provide artifacts? We need to see the SOC report excerpt and the ISO scope doc. Also network diagrams for Private and Dedicated.
[02:21] Jordan: Yes — action item.
[02:23] Priya: Quick clarifying q: For the audit logs, you said export to S3 — do you want continuous streaming or periodic exports?
[02:31] Maya: Continuous streaming would be ideal. We need near-real-time access and daily exports to our security lake. Retention-wise, legal wants one year, with on-demand extension.
[02:41] Jordan: Noted. We'll show the export pipeline and options.
[02:45] Tomás: For the POC success criteria, aside from security gating, what are the perf KPIs?
[02:50] Priya: Proposed KPIs: p95 latency under 300ms for median token loads (150 tokens), p95 under 1s for 1k tokens, throughput support of 50–75 reqs/s sustained with <10% tail latency variance, and end-to-end cost per 1k tokens within 20% of your target. Also correctness/quality: 95% of prompts should meet your evaluation rubric—Leila will provide that.
[03:16] Leila: Yup, I'll share the rubric. We'll run a quality eval against a set of 1k prompts.
[03:22] Abe (SRE): For sizing, do you recommend Dedicated GPUs for the POC or we test on hosted first?
[03:28] Priya: Typically we run the first pass on hosted so we can baseline latency and config, then spin up a small Dedicated pool to test sustained throughput and KV cache behaviors. Dedicated helps with predictable tail latency.
[03:38] Jordan: Also, Private (VPC/on-prem) option is available if you need full network control, but that adds setup time—usually 4–6 weeks. For the POC scope we can hit security gates with hosted + dedicated capacity.
[03:51] Maya: 4–6 weeks on Private is a little long; our preference is hosted w/ VPC peering and strong RBAC for pilot, then evaluate Private for GA.
[04:01] Priya: Works. On benchmarks: we'll include a KV cache warmup test, prefix caching scenarios, and burst/steady-state runs. We'll run batches with sizes 1, 4, 8 to estimate batching impact.
[04:13] Tomás: For model—do you have a recommended model family? We want a balance of latency/cost and the quality must hit our rubric.
[04:20] Priya: We'll propose 2 model variants—one quantized for cost (lower accuracy but faster), one full precision. We'll measure quality delta as part of the benchmark. Also we can test a smaller context-optimized model for short queries.
[04:33] Maya: About SSO — we use Okta. We need SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning and user groups mapped to RBAC roles. Does Redwood support SCIM?
[04:43] Jordan: Yes, SCIM provisioning and group sync are supported. Mapping groups to roles in the Console is possible — Priya can demo that in the next call.
[04:52] Priya: I'll include a short demo of SAML + SCIM mapping in week 2.
[04:56] Leila: On data handling — we need assurance that prompts / PII are not used for training, and that logs can be redacted. Is there an option to opt out of telemetry ingestion?
[05:07] Jordan: For hosted we have a privacy mode for pilot customers that disables model training ingestion and redacts PII in logs. For Private, all telemetry stays in-customer. We'll include the privacy mode details.
[05:19] Maya: Good. Also want to confirm encryption at rest for model caches and encrypt-in-transit for internal links — TLS etc.
[05:27] Jordan: Yes, TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 for at-rest; for Private, you can use your KMS.
[05:33] Tomás: Timeline—you're proposing 6 weeks?
[05:36] Priya: Here's a proposed plan: Week 0 (this week): align on artifacts and workload. Week 1: Redwood runs hosted baseline and security packet delivered. Week 2: Dedicated pool spin-up + initial benchmark. Week 3–4: Iteration, quality eval, and tuning. Week 5: Final acceptance runs. Week 6: Wrap and go/no-go decision.
[05:53] Maya: Sounds reasonable, but we may want earlier audit evidence before Week 1 complete.
[05:58] Jordan: We'll prioritize sending SOC excerpts ASAP.
[06:01] Abe: Regarding network, can you support private endpoints and IP allowlists?
[06:06] Jordan: Yes — IP allowlists and VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. Hosted public endpoints also have IP-restricted gateway options.
[06:15] Tomás: Cost-estimation—how will we model cost per 1k tokens?
[06:20] Priya: We'll produce a cost model in the benchmark report: tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batching benefits, and projected monthly cost at your expected traffic. We'll provide both hosted and Dedicated estimates.
[06:32] Leila: For benchmarking accuracy, what observability do we get? Token-level traces, latency histograms, per-route cost?
[06:39] Jordan: Console provides token-level breakdown, per-route latency, cost by token, and traces. We'll share a demo dashboard.
[06:47] Maya: And audit logs—are they tamper-evident? We need an append-only trail and integrity checks.
[06:54] Jordan: Logs are delivered with checksums and we support pushing to your S3 with lifecycle policies. For Private we can integrate with your SIEM.
[07:03] Priya: Any blockers from your side to start?
[07:06] Leila: We need to re-confirm legal for pilot data sharing but OK to proceed with test data. We'll get the prompt corpus and traces by 2026-04-11.
[07:15] Maya: I'll review the SOC artifacts once you send them. Also want to schedule a compliance deep-dive if required.
[07:21] Jordan: We'll do that — likely a 60-min session with security engineering.
[07:25] Tomás: Can we add a metric for model availability during the POC? We want 99.5% uptime for the control plane for the pilot.
[07:34] Jordan: We can set an SLA for Dedicated; for hosted the standard pilot uptime should be fine but we'll document expectations.
[07:41] Priya: Ok last items—are there any regulatory constraints (data residency) we need to be aware of?
[07:46] Maya: EU data must stay in EU region for certain customers; we need regional routing.
[07:51] Jordan: Region pinning is supported and we'll include region routing in the config.
[07:56] Tomás: Thanks everyone. Quick recap?
[08:00] Jordan: Recap: Redwood will send security artifacts, network diagrams, and benchmark plan. Priya will run baseline hosted benchmarks and demo SAML/SCIM mapping. Ember provides workload traces and prompt set. Follow-up benchmark review scheduled week of 2026-04-20.
[08:20] Maya: I'll expect SOC excerpts and ISO scope by Monday.
[08:24] Jordan: On it. Thanks all.
